exposure: Pre-gestational diabetes (Type I or Type II)
cohort: The study included 152 women with singleton pregnancies and pre-gestational type I or type II diabetes who attended antenatal care at Tuen Mun Hospital between September 1, 2017, and March 31, 2022.
finding: The rate of emergency Caesarean sections and neonatal hypoglycaemia significantly increased during the COVID-19 pandemic among women with pre-gestational diabetes, despite similar compliance with antenatal visits and other maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to the pre-pandemic period.
mod_finding: The pandemic group had significantly higher rates of emergency Caesarean sections (44.6% vs 23.5%, p=0.010) compared to the pre-pandemic group.
birth_weight: Large and small for gestational age were analysed, implying birth weight categories were considered.
gest_age: Preterm birth (birth at <37 weeks of gestation) was an outcome measured.
